name: FDA import alert red lists: firms subject to detention without physical examination
description: Which foreign manufacturers, shippers and growers are on an FDA import alert red list, meaning every shipment from them is detained without physical examination (DWPE) at the US border. Each record is one firm on one import alert, with the firm name and address as FDA prints it, the country, the date FDA published the listing, and the product codes and product descriptions it covers. Answers 'is my supplier on an FDA import alert', 'is [firm] on the red list for import alert 66-41', 'why was my shipment detained without examination', 'which firms are on the FDA red list for undeclared pharmaceutical ingredients in supplements', and 'how do I check a Chinese manufacturer before ordering'. FDA publishes 153 separate import alerts as individual current-state pages with no cross-alert firm index, so answering 'is this firm flagged anywhere' means opening 153 pages; and firms are removed from red lists on petition with no record of the removal published at all, so an assistant answering from memory names firms that were delisted years ago.
licence: Facts extracted from FDA's freely published import alert pages on accessdata.fda.gov. US government work; firm names, addresses, product codes, publication dates and FDA's stated reasons are facts and not copyrightable. Each record links back to the import alert page it was read from. Note the disclaimer FDA prints on every alert and which every record page should carry: 'This import alert represents the Agency's current guidance to FDA field personnel regarding the manufacturer(s) and/or products(s) at issue. It does not create or confer any rights for or on any person, and does not operate to bind FDA or the public.'
note: Served in parts: no single file may exceed Cloudflare's 25 MB. Concatenate the `records` arrays of the parts below.

records.notes: ***Charges: 403(i)(2), 403(q)(5)(F), 403(y). Specifically: In the "other" section of the product's ingredient list, the product lists "Trade Secret Stabilization Process" and "Solubilized in water from the Austrian Alps." While these may be true statements, the former is not appropriate to list in the ingredients section of the product and the latter is not the common or usual name for "water." Additionally, ingredients such as NADH, Q10H2, Pyridoxal- 5'-PO43, and Vitamin B2 RSP must be spelled out or listed by their common and usual names. The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403 (q)(5)(F) of the Act in that your "Supplement Facts" panel is not in an appropriate format as required by 21 CFR 101.36. The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403 (y) [21 U.S.C. § 343(y)] of the Act. The label fails to bear a domestic address or domestic phone number through which the responsible person, as described in section 761 [21 U.S.C. § 379aa-1] of the Act, may receive a report of a serious adverse event with such dietary supplement. ***

records.firm_address: Maale Adumim, Yerushalayim , 15, Kharuvit , Ma'Ale Adumim, ISRAEL
records.product_code: 20 D - - 09 Grape Juice, Berry Juice or Concentrates
records.notes: Violation(s): The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(i)(2) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(i)(2)] because the article purports to be a beverage containing fruit or vegetable juice and the label fails to bear a percent juice declaration as required by 21 CFR 101.30. Also, the article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(a)(1) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(a)(1)] because the product is false and misleading in that it bears a Natural claim but fails to meet the requirements to bear such claim. FDA has not established a regulatory definition for the term natural; however, the Agency has a long-standing policy that restricts the use of the term ¿natural¿ when a product is formulated with added color, synthetic substances, and flavors as stated in 21 CFR 101.22 (see 58 FR 2407 (January 6, 1993)). Among other things, this policy states that the term natural means that nothing artificial or synthetic (including all color additives regardless of source) has been included in, or has been added to, a food that would not normally be expected to be in the food. This product appears to contain sulfur dioxide, which is listed in the ingredient statement as a preservative. Therefore, the product name can not include the term Natural. The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) in that it is misbranded within the meaning of section 403(e)(1) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(e)(1)] because the product label does not contain a complete name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor in accordance with 21 CFR 101.5. ; 4/3/2012

records.notes: The product is labeled as containing 50 mg of Mucuna pruriens seed extract, which itself is characterized as 98% L-DOPA. L-DOPA is an endogenous precursor to dopamine, but when given exogenously, it is associated with a number of adverse reactions, such as nausea, vomiting, effects on blood pressure and heart rhythm, and neurological and psychiatric side effects. The product is labeled as containing added folate [specifically L-5-methyltetrahydrofolate (L-5-methyl-THF)] at two-times the total daily recommended intake for adults. For much of the U.S. population, background dietary exposure to folates is near or above the tolerable upper intake limit set by the National Academy of Medicine. FDA has no basis to conclude as GRAS uses of folates that further increase cumulative dietary exposure to folates. FDA is not aware of any applicable listed exception for the use of L-5-methyl-THF in this product. These uses of L-DOPA and L-5-methyl-THF are food additives, and food additives are deemed unsafe unless they are used in conformity with a regulation authorizing their use. No food additive regulation authorizes the use of L-DOPA or L-5-methyl-THF as ingredients in an energy drink. Examples of claims observed on the firm's social media website that establish the intended use of "PT-141" include, but may not be limited to, the following: On the CanLab Research Facebook social media account, on June 24, 2019, the firm posted a chromatogram report under the heading "PT-141: 98.24%." A commenter named Joel Grotrian asked "May i (sic) ask what this means and what this peptide does?" and a commenter named Michael Shofield replied "[I]t will give you a hard-on for an entire day." Under section 505(a) of the FD&C Act, a new drug may not be legally marketed in the United States without an FDA-approved application. records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(q) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(q)]. Nutrition Facts label is not in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(ii). The label makes the claim, "containing high level of vitamin B6"; however, vitamin B6 is not listed in the Nutrition Facts. [21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iv]. Vitamin B6 must be sufficient for the label to qualify to bear the claim, 21 CFR 101.13(b) and 21 CFR 101.54. Vitamins A and C are not declared [21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(ii)]. Missing 'servings per container' and fat as "fat, total," or "total fat," and combines the %DV for saturate fat and trans-fat, which is not permitted. Missing "dietary fiber," and lists nutrients in incorrect order. [21 CFR 101.9(c) and (d)]. The Nutrition Facts label fails to bear the correct footnote as listed in 21 CFR 101.9(d)(9). The statement, "*5% or less is a little, 15% or more is a lot," which is not permitted. The Nutrition Facts label not formatted correctly. 21 CFR 101.9 does not provide for another country's nutrition label on products sold in the US. Section 403(r)(1)(A). The website Jardimdegaia.com, listed on the product label, bears the claim "very rich in antioxidants." Claim does not comply with 21 CFR 101.54(g). "Antioxidant" must include the nutrient source and reference daily intake (RDI) must have been established (21 CFR 101.54(g)(1), and the nutrients must have recognized antioxidant activity (21 CFR 101.54(g)(2). Each nutrient must be sufficient to qualify for claim under 21 CFR 101.54(b), (c), or (e), (21 CFR 101.54(g)(3). "Antioxidant" must include names of the nutrients in the claim or, "antioxidant" or "antioxidants" may be linked by a symbol (e.g., an asterisk), followed by the name ofnutrients with recognized antioxidant activity [21 CFR 101.54(g)(4)].

records.notes: Product appears to be is a drug, as per section 201(g)(1) of the FDCA, 21U.S.C.321(g)(1), and an unapproved new drug, as per section 505(a) of the FDCA, 21U.S.C.355(a). Claims on LBL (21CFR201.128) include: "Fights 7 Dental Problems, Cavities, Bad Breath, Bleeding Gums, Toothache, Yellowing, Plaque, Germs...antiseptic and antibacterial properties...anti-inflammatory". Based on the claims, the product is a drug as defined by section 201(g)(1)(B) of the FDCA, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(B), because it is intended for the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease, and/or under section 201(g)(1)(C) of the FDCA, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(C), because it is intended to affect the structure or any function of the body. Specifically, it is intended for use as an anticaries, oral healthcare analgesic, oral antiseptic, and antiplaque/antigingivitic drug product. OTC drug products intended for use as anticaries are subject to the final rule for Anticaries Drug Products for OTC Human Use (anticaries final rule), 21CFR355. However, it is not labeled or formulated in accordance with this final rule for the reasons explained below. Product is a four-way combination drug product because it is intended for use as an anticaries, oral healthcare analgesic, oral antiseptic, and antiplaque/antigingivitic drug product. The anticaries final rule does not permit a four-way combination drug product such as this product. Thus, as formulated and labeled, it does not comply with the final rule described above. Furthermore, we are not aware of sufficient evidence to show the product as formulated and labeled, is GRAS and effective. Therefore, it appears to be a new drug within the meaning of section 201(p) of the FDCA, 21U.S.C. 321(p). Under sections 505(a) and 301(d) of the FDCA, a new drug may not be introduced/delivered for introduction into interstate commerce unless an FDA-approved application is in effect for it. records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of the following sections of the FD&C Act: Section 403(e)(1) - the label fails to list the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor in accordance with 21 CFR 101.5. Section 403(q) - the nutrition information is not in accordance to 21 CFR 101.9. Specifically, • The label appears to make claims for cholesterol and fatty acids ("cholesterol free" and "low fat"), yet it fails to declare the monounsaturated fat and polyunsaturated fat content as is required by 21 CFR 101.9(c)(2). • The label fails to declare the percent daily value for protein as required by 101.9(c)(7)(i). Section 403(r)(1)(A) - the labeling bears unauthorized nutrient content claims. For example: • "High in fiber"; The dietary fiber content does not meet the 10-19% of the Reference Daily Intake (RDI) or Daily Reference Value (DRV) per reference amount customarily consumed. • "[A] good source of Protein...and Isoflavones" is an unauthorized claim because there are no established RDI's or DRV's for this substance. • The label fails to declare a value for Omega-3 alpha-linolenic. • The product does not meet the requirements under 21 CFR 101.62(b) for a "low fat" claim. • The product claims "low sodium" and "cholesterol free", however per 21 CFR 101.13(e)(2), soybeans are naturally this way. Section 403(r)(1)(B) - the label bears an unauthorized health claim. The label has a heart symbol with a checkmark near the nutrient content claims on the product label. This is an implied health claim for cardiovascular disease. This claim does not meet the requirements to make these claims because the required language is not being used.

records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) for the following: It appears to be misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(c)(f) of the Food, Drug, & Cosmetic Act (the Act) [21 U.S.C. § 343(e)(1)] in that the food is in package form and the label fails to bear the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor in accordance with 21 CFR 101.5. It appears to be misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(f) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(f)] in that any word, statement, or other information required by or under the authority of the FD&C Act to appear on the label or labeling is not prominently placed thereon with such conspicuousness (as compared with other words, statements, designs, or devices, in the labeling) and in such terms as to render it likely to be read and understood by the ordinary individual under customary terms of purchase and use (for example, label contains information in two or more languages but fails to repeat all required information in both languages in accordance with 21 CFR 101.15(c) (2), or label fails to include all required information in English in accordance with 21 CFR 101.15(c)(1), except in the case of articles distributed solely in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico or in a Territory where the predominant language is one other than English)). Specifically, the single product unit containers do not contain all information in both English and the foreign language(s). Other labeling violations were also noted as follows; The principal display panel of a food in a package form shall bear as one of its principal features a statement of the identity of the commodity in accordance with 21 CFR 101.3(a). It appears the statement of identity on the label applied to the outer plastic shrink wrap covering of the multiunit package, Sweet Fruit Drink (Apple), and the one on the single product unit containers, Demi Soda Apple, are different.

records.notes: VIOLATION (IN NOTES): 1. 403(q) ; 403(i)(2) 1. The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(q) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(q)] because the label fails to bear nutrition labeling (Supplement Facts panel) in the proper format, which is required under 21 CFR 101.36. For example: The caloric content is expressed in kcal rather than Calories. The Percent Daily Value for dietary ingredients that have a Reference Daily Intake (RDI) or a Daily Reference Value (DRV) are not declared. Specifically, the product does not list the percent daily values for Vitamin A, Vitamin C, Vitamin D, Vitamin E, thiamin(Vitamin B1), niacin (Vitamin B3), folate (folic acid), Vitamin B12, pantothenic acid as required by 21 CFR 101.36(b)(2)(iii). The quantitative amount by weight per serving for each dietary ingredient are not declared as required by 21 CFR 101.36(b)(2) and 101.36(b)(3). The correct nomenclature for some of the dietary ingredients is not declared, as required by 21 CFR 101.36(b)(2)(B). For example, niacin is incorrectly listed as nicotinamide. The dietary ingredients are not listed in the proper order. Specifically, Vitamin B6, Vitamin E, sodium, Vitamin C, niacin, pantothenic acid, thiamin, folic acid, Vitamin B12, Vitamin A, and Vitamin Dare not in the correct order, as required by 21 CFR 10 1.36(b )(2)(i)(B).

Products are declared as “Amomum Villosum,” “Cordeceps Flower” and “Dried Fructus Pyri,” not “Dried Fruit – Fructus Amomi,” “Cordiceps Mushrooms” not “Dried Pears.” the declared quantitative amount, of Iron for all products and Calcium for Cordiceps Mushrooms, Dried Pears, and Dried Fruit, declared in the Nutrition Facts label appears to be incorrect, based of FDA laboratory analysis. When a vitamin, mineral, protein, total carbohydrate, polyunsaturated or monounsaturated fat, or dietary fiber meets the definition of a Class II nutrient, the nutrient content of the composite must be at least equal to 80 percent of the value declared on the label. Provided, that no regulatory action will be based on a determination of a nutrient value that falls below this level by a factor less than the variability generally recognized for the analytical method used in that food at the level involved. (21 CFR 101.9(g)(4)(ii)). The principal display panel does not appear to include the statement of identity in accordance 21 CFR 101.3. records.notes: Article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded within section 403(k) of the FD&C Act. Ingredient list declares preservatives but does not declare their function, as is required under 21 CFR 101.22(j). Article is subject to refusal pursuant to section 801(a)(3) as it appears to be misbranded within section 403(q) of the FD&C Act. Nutrition information is not in the correct format as required by 21 CFR 101.9. • Total carbohydrate is declared as 0.3g. A statement of the number of grams of total carbohydrate must be expressed to the nearest gram, except that if a serving contains less than 1 gram, "Contains less than 1 gram" or "less than 1 gram" may be used, or if the serving contains less than 0.5 gram, the content may be expressed as zero [21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)]. • Calorie content is incorrectly declared. For the carbohydrates, fat, and protein amounts declared and the guidelines provided in 21 CFR 101.9(c)(i), the product cannot mathematically provide 100 Calories. • %DV for sodium declared as 108%. Based on the amount of sodium in a serving declared on the label (2180 mg) and the DRV for sodium (2400 mg), the %DV for sodium is incorrect. Article is subject to refusal pursuant to section 801(a)(3) as it appears to be misbranded within section 403(i)(1) of the FD&C Act. Label fails to bear the common or usual name as required by 21 CFR 101.3(b). Article is subject to refusal pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) as it appears to be misbranded within section 403(e)(1) of the FD&C Act. Labeling fails to list the place of business of manufacturer, packer, or distributor as required by 21 CFR 101.5(d).

records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (the Act) in that each component product appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(i)(2) in that the component product labels fail to declare all the common or usual names of each ingredient. The ingredient list or other ingredient list of each component product label fails to be placed below the Supplement Facts label. Product label declares “HPMC” as an ingredient but does not list the common or usual name of that ingredient. The standardized common name (SCN) of each botanical dietary ingredient, is not listed in the Supplement Facts label. Section 403(q)(5)(F) in that the presentation of the nutrition information on the labeling of the product does not comply with 21 CFR 101.36. The label fails to declare the quantitative amount of calories per serving in the Supplement Facts label. The quantitative amount of the declared dietary ingredient fails to be expressed using metric measures in appropriate units (i.e., 1000 or more units must be declared in the next higher set of units, e.g., 1,100 mg, must be declared as 1.1 g). Label fails to declare “Supplement Facts” on the full width of the nutrition label (Supplement Facts label). | The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (the Act) in that each component product appears to be misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(i)(2) in that the component product labels fail to declare all the common or usual names of each ingredient. records.notes: Problem(s): FDA inspection found serious deviations of the seafood HACCP regulation (21 CFR Part 123). On November 30 and December 1, 2025, and February 5, 2026, the firm responded to the violative inspection, conducted November 12 to 13, 2025, which included a revised HACCP plan. Based on the inspectional findings and review of the firm’s response, FDA has determined the listed seafood products processed in the facility appear adulterated within the meaning of section 402(a)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (the Act). Specific violations include: 21 CFR 123.6(c)(2) – HACCP plan does not list the following critical control points: packaging critical control point to control Clostridium botulinum in reduced oxygen packaging of plastic jars; unrefrigerated processing critical control point for processing steps such as thawing, washing, and packaging to control pathogenic bacteria growth and toxin formation; packaging critical control point to control undeclared allergens and food intolerance substance ingredients; and receiving critical control point to control environmental chemical contaminants in raw crabs. | Problem(s): FDA inspection found serious deviations of the seafood HACCP regulation (21 CFR Part 123). records.product_description: Winter Shot Powder with Ginger; Echinacea and Tibet Mushroom (Code 3373)
records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that the product appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(q) of the Act in that the presentation of the nutrition information on the labeling of product does not comply with 21 CFR 101.36. Supplement Facts label incorrectly declares sodium with 10mg and 0% Daily Value. Dietary ingredients for which DRV’s have been established, “Less than 1%” or “<1%” must be used to declare the “% Daily Value” when rounded to the nearest percent is zero (21 CFR 101.36(b)(2)(iii)(C)). Supplement Facts label incorrectly declares Vitamin A and choline with a % Daily Value of <1% and 1%, respectively. (21 CFR 101.36(b)(2)(i)). Declaration for folate must be in mcg DFE (when expressed as a quantitative amount by weight in a conventional food or a dietary supplement), and percent DV based on folate in mcg DFE. When folic acid is added or when a claim is made about the nutrient, folic acid must be declared in parentheses, as mcg of folic acid. (21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iv), table, footnote 6). Declared 18% Daily Value for copper is incorrect (21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)). Label incorrectly declares a % Daily Value for Total Sugars in that there is no Daily Value established for Total Sugars. For declared subcomponents that have no DRV’s, a symbol (e.g., an asterisk) must be placed in the “Percent Daily Value” column that refers to the same symbol at the bottom of the nutrition label, below the last heavy bar and inside the box and followed by the statement “Daily Value not established”. The “Includes 5g added sugars” fails to be indented under Total Sugars and to declare the % Daily Value for added sugars. (21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)(ii), 101.9(c)(9), 101.36(b)(2)(i), and 101.36(b)(2)(iii)(F)). Section 403(e)(2) of the Act. Outer package label fails to adequately declare the net quantity of contents on the principal display panel (21 CFR 101.7).

Article is subject to refusal pursuant to section 801(a)(3) as it appears to be misbranded within section 403(q) of the FD&C Act. Nutrition information is not in the correct format as required by 21 CFR 101.9. • Total carbohydrate is declared as 0.3g. A statement of the number of grams of total carbohydrate must be expressed to the nearest gram, except that if a serving contains less than 1 gram, "Contains less than 1 gram" or "less than 1 gram" may be used, or if the serving contains less than 0.5 gram, the content may be expressed as zero [21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)]. • Calorie content is incorrectly declared. For the carbohydrates, fat, and protein amounts declared and the guidelines provided in 21 CFR 101.9(c)(i), the product cannot mathematically provide 100 Calories. • %DV for sodium declared as 108%. Based on the amount of sodium in a serving declared on the label (2180 mg) and the DRV for sodium (2400 mg), the %DV for sodium is incorrect. Article is subject to refusal pursuant to section 801(a)(3) as it appears to be misbranded within section 403(i)(1) of the FD&C Act. Label fails to bear the common or usual name as required by 21 CFR 101.3(b). Article is subject to refusal pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) as it appears to be misbranded within section 403(e)(1) of the FD&C Act. Labeling fails to list the place of business of manufacturer, packer, or distributor as required by 21 CFR 101.5(d).

records.notes: VIOLATION (IN NOTES): 1. 403(q) and 2. 403(i)(2) 1. The product fails to properly declare the serving size as specified by 21 CFR 101.9(b) and 101.12(b). Specifically, the product declares the serving size as 3.50z (l00 gr); however the established Reference Amount Customarily Consumed (RACC) for All other candies [21 CFR 101.12(b), Table 2, under Sugars and Sweets] is 40 g. Therefore, the nutrition information is not correct because it is not based on the established RACC provided for this product; The serving size is not expressed in a common household measure as required by 21 CFR 101.9(b)(5) and the "Servings Per Container" is not consistent with the requirements under 21 CFR 101.9(b)(8); The product fails to meet the requirements of 21 CFR 101.9(c) for the declaration of the required nutrients, the level of those nutrients, and the specified order of those nutrients. Specifically, the nutrition label fails to declare: calories from fat, saturated fat, trans fat, cholesterol, sodium, dietary fiber, sugars, vitamin A, vitamin C, calcium, and iron. "Organic acid" is not permitted to be declared in the nutrition label. Also, protein must be declared after carbohydrate on the nutrition label. "Carbohydrate" must be declared as "Carbohydrate, total" or "Total carbohydrate"; The quantitative amounts of the declared nutrients are not rounded in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(c) and the amounts are declared using commas instead of decimal points;¿ The nutrition information is not provided in the format specified by 21 CFR 101.9. For example, the full footnote is not provided in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(d)(9)(i). Also, the nutrition label declares "gr" rather than the appropriate abbreviation, "g", for grams [21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(i)]. In addition, the nutrition label fails to list the numerical percent of the DRV in a column aligned under the heading "% DV" as required per 21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii).

records.import_alert_name: Detention Without Physical Examination of Imported Food Products That Appear to Be Misbranded
records.firm_address: Number 12 Industrial Avenue, New District, Huanggang Town , Kaiping , Jiangmen City, Guangdong Province CHINA
records.product_code: 03 A - - 03 Biscuits
records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(q) of the FD&C Act in that the label or labeling fails to bear the required nutrition information (21 CFR 101.9). Serving size is declared as “1 Serving Per Container” and “100g,” but the net weight of the entire package is only 52g. Section 403(f) of the Act in that product label contains information in two languages but does not repeat all the required information in both languages 21 CFR 101.15(c)(2). Section 403(i)(1) of the Act in that the product label fails to bear the common or usual name of the food as required by 21 CFR 101.3(b). Principal Display Panel states the product is an “Ox Ear Biscuit” and the label attached to the information panel says “biscuit.” In North America, a biscuit is a small, typically round cake of bread leavened with baking powder, baking soda, or sometimes yeast. Based on the product images, this product appears to be thin, and maybe even crispy, and does not represent a biscuit product in the US. Additionally, the product does not contain any “ox” ingredient; even if “ox ear” is meant to be descriptive of the product’s shape, we question if the average US consumer would not be misled by the product name as currently declared on the PDP. Section 403(i)(2) of the Act in that each ingredient is not declared by its common or usual name in accordance with 21 CFR 101.4. “Compound antioxidant” does not appear to be an appropriate and specific common or usual name for an ingredient, as required by 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1). The sub-ingredients for the red bean curd sauce include “soy sauce,” which is known to also be a multi-ingredient product; however, the sub-ingredients of the soy sauce are not listed as required by 21 CFR 101.4(b)(2)(i).

records.firm_address: Kunming National High & New Room 2nd , Floor;209 2188 No. Kegao Road , Kunming, Yunnan CHINA
records.product_code: 54 Y - - 99 Vitamin, Mineral, Proteins and Unconventional Dietary Specialities For Humans and Animals, N.E.C.
records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that the product appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(q) of the Act. Serving size declared on the label is incorrect. Serving size for a dietary supplement is the maximum amount consumed per eating occasion as recommended on the product label as defined in 21 CFR 101.9(b) and 21 CFR 101.12(b) Table 2. The article’s “Suggested Use” instructions state “For the best results, take 2-3 capsules daily, or as required”. The serving size should be 3 capsules. Nutrition information on the labeling does not comply with 21 CFR 101.36 and 101.9. “Supplements Facts”, is not set at full width of the nutrition label (21 CFR101.36(e)(1)). No provision in the regulation to include the heading “ingredients” within the Supplement Facts label. A heavy bar is not placed beneath the subheading “Servings Per Container” (21 CFR 101.36(e)(6)(i)), and beneath the final (b)(2)-dietary ingredient (21 CFR 101.36(e)(6)(ii)). Dietary ingredients that comprise the proprietary blend do not appear to be indented (21 CFR 101.36(c)(2)). Missing hairline rules centered between the lines of text to separate the dietary ingredients above from the dietary ingredients below (21 CFR 101.36(c)(2) and (e)(5)). Section 403(i)(2) of the Act. Label fails to declare all the common or usual names of each ingredient (21 CFR 101.36 and 21 CFR 101.4(h). Label lists “Panax Notoginseng”, but this is not the standardized common name (SCN) in the reference Herbs of Commerce (HOC). Section 403(s)(2)(C) of the Act. Labels fail to identify the part of the plant (e.g., root, leaves) from which each botanical dietary ingredient in the product is derived (21 CFR 101.4(h), botanical dietary ingredients “Turmeric” and “Tart Cherry” do not list the plant part.

records.notes: Nectar Supreme product is misbranded within the meaning of section 403(a) (l) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(a)(l)] in that the labels are false or misleading because the amount of nutrient present is less than the amount declared on the label. Specifically, FDA analyzed the sample of your Nectar Supreme to determine whether the nutrition information on your Nutrition Facts panel accurately reflects the nutrient content of the product. The product label states that one serving (1 113 tablespoons) contains 400 IU of Vitamin D and 100 mg of Vitamin C. However, FDA analysis found the Vitamin D content was 86.8% (original analysis) and 80.3% (check analysis) of declared value. Analysis revealed the Vitamin C content was 32.5% (original analysis) and 34% mg (check analysis) of declared value. Colageno Hidrolizado Shake, Goji-Loe, Nectar Supreme and OxiCell products are misbranded within the meaning of section 403(q)(5)(F) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(q)(5)(F)] in that the presentation of the nutrition information on the labeling of the products does not comply with 21 CFR 101.36. Published on 06/11/2015 | OxiCell product label is misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(y) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(y)] in that the label fails to bear a domestic address or domestic phone number through which the responsible person (as described in section 761) may receive a report of a serious adverse event with such dietary supplement. OxiCell product is misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(k) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(k)] in that the product bears or contains chemical preservatives, but fails to provide a separate description of the function of these ingredients as required. In accordance with 21 CFR 10 1.22(j), the label of a food to which a chemical preservative has been added shall bear a declaration of both the common or usual name of the ingredient and a separate description of its function, e.g., "preservative." records.notes: Charge: 403(i)(1) • The Lotte European Waffles (1.41 oz. and 5.64 oz.) sold to individual customers are misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(i)(1) of the Act [21 U.S.C. 343(i)(1)] because there is no accurate statement of identity on the Principal Display Panel, as required under 21 CFR 101.3. We question the name of the product "Lotte Waffle" being an appropriately descriptive term or when the nature of the food is obvious, a fanciful name commonly used by the public for such food within the meaning of sections 21 CFR 101.3(b) and 21 CFR 102.5(a). The common or usual name of a food, which may be a coined term, shall accurately identify or describe, in as simple and direct terms as possible, the basic nature of the food or its characterizing properties or ingredients. It appears that this product is not generally recognized by American consumers as a waffle, but may be similar to a snack cracker or cookie product. We also note that the statement of identity must be consistent wherever it appears on the label. Charge: 403(i)(2) • The Lotte European Waffles (1.41 oz. and 5.64 oz.) are misbranded within the meaning of section 403(i)(2) of the Act [21 U.S.C. 343(i) (2)] because they are fabricated from two or more ingredients but the labels fail to declare the common or usual name of each ingredient, as required under 21 CFR 101.4. records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that the product appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(a)(1) of the FD&C Act. Labeling is false or misleading in any particular., the "Statement of Identity" must be the common or usual name of the food (21 CFR 101.3). In addition, the product is labeled as “Honey” and appears to also bear the claim “100% pure bee honey”. Section 403(i)(1) of the FD&C Act. Product is labeled as “Honey” and appears to bear the claim “100% pure bee honey”; however, FDA lab results support the presence of added C-4 sugars. Section 403(e)(1) of the FD&C Act. Label fails to bear the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor (21 CFR 101.5). Label shows: “Imported by: Amexim Inc.” and a website; however, it does not appear to include the complete place of business. Online information cannot be used in lieu of the required address information, which must include the street address, city, State, and ZIP code in accordance with 21 CFR 101.5. Section 403(q) of the FD&C Act. Nutrition information does not declare added sugars and does not appear to declare Vitamin D and potassium, which are required nutrients under 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8). Labeling declares “Total Sugars 16 g” but does not declare added sugars.

records.notes: Nectar Supreme product is misbranded within the meaning of section 403(a) (l) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(a)(l)] in that the labels are false or misleading because the amount of nutrient present is less than the amount declared on the label. Specifically, FDA analyzed the sample of your Nectar Supreme to determine whether the nutrition information on your Nutrition Facts panel accurately reflects the nutrient content of the product. The product label states that one serving (1 113 tablespoons) contains 400 IU of Vitamin D and 100 mg of Vitamin C. However, FDA analysis found the Vitamin D content was 86.8% (original analysis) and 80.3% (check analysis) of declared value. Analysis revealed the Vitamin C content was 32.5% (original analysis) and 34% mg (check analysis) of declared value. OxiCell product is misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(k) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(k)] in that the product bears or contains chemical preservatives, but fails to provide a separate description of the function of these ingredients as required. records.notes: The article appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(q) because the nutrition label does not meet the requirements of 21 CFR 101.9: The product fails to properly declare the serving size as specified by 21 CFR 101.9 (b) and 101.12(b); therefore, the nutrition information is not correct. The nutrition label fails to declare all of the required nutrition information in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(c). Specifically, the nutrition label has five nutrients missing (trans fat, vitamin A, vitamin C, calcium, and iron). FDA could not determine label format, in that, it appears the product could qualify for the simplified format of the nutrition label, which requires the product to contain insignificant amounts of eight or more of the nutrients listed in 21 CFR 101.9(f) and placement of an asterisk at the bottom of the label followed by the statement "Percent Daily Values are based on a 2,000 calorie diet" when the footnote is omitted [21 CFR 101.9(f)(5)]. The product label is further misbranded, in that, the quantitative amounts for total fat, saturated fat, total carbohydrate, and protein are not in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(i). Specifically, the nutrient amount should be appended with a "g" for grams. The product label is further misbranded within the meaning of section 403(f) because all required words, statements and other information on the label must be included in both languages. The place of business is only in English. (21 CFR 101.15 (c)(1))

At 2 percent or less, they may be grouped and expressed per 21 CFR 101.4(a)(2). “E” numbers are not permitted (21 CFR 101.4). “Hydrolysed” is not the English spelling for “hydrolyzed.” Section 403(q) of the Act. Nutrition Facts label (NFL) does not comply with 21 CFR 101.9. NFL of the multi-unit packages not consistent with NFL of individual units for Iron (21 CFR 101.9(c). The individual units include a no-permitted foreign NFL (21 CFR 101.9). The saturated fat and trans fat not expressed to the nearest 0.5-gram (21 CFR 101.9(c)(2)(i) and (ii)). records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(q) in that the nutrition information is incomplete and does not meet the formatting requirements specified under 21 CFR 101.9. Section 403(i)(2) in that it is fabricated from two or more ingredients and the label fails to bear the common or usual name of each such ingredients for: Hydrolysed groundnut protein, vegetable oil (21 CFR 101.4(b)(4) and mineral (170(i)), edible starch, acidifying agent (330), Flavour enhancers (627 & 631) and raising agent (500 (ii)). Section 403(e)(2) in that the food is in package form and the label fails to bear an accurate statement of the quantity of the contents in terms of weight, measure, or numerical count. Section 403(f) in that the label contains information in two or more languages but fails to repeat all required information in both languages in accordance with 21 CFR 101.15(c)(2).

records.notes: The Fish Dumpling products are subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) in that they appear to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(f) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(f)] because the products label contains information in two languages, but does not repeat all the required information in both languages. As required by 21 CFR 101.15(c)(2), if a product label contains any representation in a foreign language, all words, statements, and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the label must appear in the foreign language. Specifically, these products fail to declare the nutrition information in the foreign language The Fish Dumpling products are subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) in that they appear to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(q) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(q)] because the nutrition information does not comply with 21 CFR 101.9. Specifically, the serving sizes do not appear to be based on the appropriate reference amount customarily consumed (RACC) [21 CFR 101.9(b)(2) and 101.12(b)(Table 2)]. The products appear to fall under the "Entrees without sauce, e.g. plain..." category which has a RACC of 85g cooked; 110g uncooked. records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(f) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(f)] because it contains information in a second language, Spanish; therefore, all required information must be in both languages (i.e., the English language as well as the foreign language). Statement of identity must be declared in both the foreign language and English as required by 21 CFR 101.15(c)(2). inner unit containers are not exempt from the bilingual labeling requirements in 21 CFR 101.15(c)(2). exemptions in 21 CFR 1.24(a)(14) do not extend to the labeling requirements in 21 CFR 101.15 and section 403(w) of the Act. Section 403(i)(2) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(i)(2)] in that the product is fabricated from two or more ingredients and the common or usual name of each ingredient is not declared on the label, as required under 21 CFR 101.4. Missing lentils as sub-ingredients for “chocolate flavored lentils”. Vegetable shortening does not list vegetable source of the shortening. [21 CFR 101.4(b)(14)]. Product label lists the percent of the ingredient before the listing of the intended ingredient and it is not listed parenthetically. [21 CFR 101.4(e)]. English translation of outer package label shows: whey powder, carob flour, lazicar, solid green FCF, talc. e. Buttermilk is declared on the outer label, but based on the google translation, but not declared on the individual units. records.firm_address: Quintana Roo 1611 , Col. Guadalupana , Guadalajara, Jalisco MEXICO
records.product_code: 33 Y - - 99 Candy Without Chocolate N.E.C.
records.product_description: Botu 2 Lollipop with Chili Powder (Assort Fruit Flavors)
records.notes: VIOLATION (IN NOTES): 1. 403(q) 1. The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that it appears to be misbranded product within the meaning of Section 403(q) of the Act [21 U.S.C. 343(q)] in that the nutrition facts information is not in an appropriate format as defined in 21 CFR 101.9. For example: The Caloric content is not declared in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(c)(l). Specifically, the caloric content should be declared as "Calories" and the units should be in calories, not "k" or "kcal." The "Energy Content" may be expressed in kilojoules units, added in parentheses immediately following the statement of caloric content. The Trans fat content is not declared as required by 21 CFR 101.9(c)(2)(ii). The Calcium and Iron content is not declared as required by 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8) (ii)..

In accordance with section 21CFR101.15(c)(2),if a LBL contains any representation in a foreign language, all words,statements,and other information required by or under authority of the Act to appear on the LBL must appear in the foreign language. Specifically,the product fails to list the nutrition information and ingredient statement in the foreign language. We also note that the product fails to declare the statement of identity (SOI) in the English language as required by section 21CFR 101.15(c)(1). Section 403(i)(2) of the FDCA [21 U.S.C. 343(i)(2)]-the LBL fails to declare the sub-ingredients for an ingredient which contains two or more ingredients,as required under section 21CFR101.4(b). For example,the ingredient statement lists "Fish sauce" and "Garlic juice"; however,it appears the sub-ingredients are not declared. The requirement to list these component ingredients (or "sub- ingredients") may be met by either parenthetically listing the component ingredients after the common or usual name of the main ingredient,or by listing the component ingredients without listing the ingredient itself. Under the first alternative,the component ingredients must be listed in descending order of predominance within the multi-component ingredient;and under the second alternative,the component ingredients must be listed in descending order of predominance in the finished food.

For example: The serving declaration, 25g is not in expressed in common household measure. The Total Calorie content is not expressed to the nearest 10-calorie increment [21 CFR 101.9(c)(1)] The Saturated Fat content should be expressed as zero when a serving contains less that 0.5- grams of saturated fat [ 21 CFR 101.9(c)(2)(i)] The Cholesterol content should be expressed to the nearest milligram [21 CFR 101.9(c)(3)] The Sodium content should be expressed in milligrams. In addition, when a serving contains less that 5-milligrams of sodium, it should be expressed as zero. [21 CFR 101.9(c)(4)] The Total carbohydrate content in a serving should be declared as Carbohydrate, total or Total carbohydrate and should be expressed in grams. [21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)] The Sugar content should be declared as Sugars. [21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)(ii)] The Protein should be expressed to the nearest gram. records.notes: *** Charges: 403(i)(2), 403(q)(5)(F), 403(y). The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(i)(2) of Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act (the Act) in that it is fabricated from two or more ingredients, but the product labels fail to declare the common or usual names of each ingredient used as required by 21 CFR 101.36. Specifically: In the "other" section of the product's ingredient list, the product lists "Trade Secret Stabilization Process" and "Solubilized in water from the Austrian Alps." While these may be true statements, the former is not appropriate to list in the ingredients section of the product and the latter is not the common or usual name for "water." Additionally, ingredients such as NADH, Q10H2, Pyridoxal- 5'-PO43, and Vitamin B2 RSP must be spelled out or listed by their common and usual names. The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403 (q)(5)(F) of the Act in that your "Supplement Facts" panel is not in an appropriate format as required by 21 CFR 101.36. The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3) of the Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403 (y) [21 U.S.C. § 343(y)] of the Act. The label fails to bear a domestic address or domestic phone number through which the responsible person, as described in section 761 [21 U.S.C. § 379aa-1] of the Act, may receive a report of a serious adverse event with such dietary supplement.***

records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(q) of the Act [21 USC §343(q)] in that the nutrition information (e.g. Nutrition Facts label) does not comply with the requirements in 21 CFR 101.9, whereby the product label fails to declare a serving size based on the reference amount customarily consumed (RACC); nutrition information lists a daily value for Calories, which is not permitted, and fails to list the daily values for fats, cholesterol, sodium, Total Carbohydrates, and dietary fiber; the footnote is not declared in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(d)(9). The Nutrition Facts heading is not set with the full width of the Nutrition Facts label. [21 CFR 101.9(d)(2)]. Section 403(i)(2) of the FD&C Act in that the product is fabricated from two or more ingredients and the ingredients are not declared appropriately, as required under 21 CFR 101.4. Vegetable protein does not list source; "Seasoning" is not the common or usual name of a food ingredient; the sub-ingredients of the parmesan cheese are not listed on the label. Note that parmesan cheese is a standardized food, 21 CFR 133.165, European "E" numbers for additives are not part of the common or usual name of these ingredients and are not permitted to be in the ingredient statement and are intervening material in this location (21 CFR 101.2(e)). Section 403(f) of the Act [21 USC §343(f)] because the product label contains information in multiple languages but does not repeat all the required information in all languages. As required by 21 CFR 101.15(c)(2), The label bears statements in French and Filipino, in addition to English. Section 403(e)(2) of the FD&C Act in that the food is in package form and the label fails to bear an accurate statement of the quantity of the contents in terms of weight, measure in US measure (avoirdupois pound(s) and ounce(s)) as required by 21 CFR 101.7.

records.product_code: 21 V - - 48 Coconut, Subtropical and Tropical Fruit, Juices, Milk, Creme, Drinks and Nectars
records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that the product appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(f) because the product label contains information in two languages but does not repeat all the required label information in both languages (21 CFR 101.15(c)). Multi unit retail container/case must include all required information in English. Section 403(e)(1) of the FD&C Act. Stick on English label does not appear to declare the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor. Section 403(e)(2) of the FD&C Act. Foreign language label for net quantity of contents indicates 245gm, the stick on English label indicates 245ml (8.64oz). Does not appear to meet the requirements in 21 CFR 101.7(s); declaration does not appear to include the total quantity of contents of the multiunit package in terms of fluid ounces. Case net quantity of contents is shows 245g x 10 on one label panel and on a sticker on the case states "N.W. 245ml (8.64oz.)." Appropriate unit of measure for a liquid (21 CFR 101.7(a)) and "N.W." is not the appropriate term for declaration of the net quantity. Section 403(a)(1) of the FD&C Act. Labeling is false or misleading because of inconsistencies in the statement of identity (21 CFR 101.3). The principal display panel on case and bottles show product as "Fresh Coconut Milk" the stick on English label on bottles and a sticker label on the case show "Coconut Water" which is two different types of coconut products. "fresh" on these labels appears to be misleading because it suggests or implies that the food is in its raw state (21 CFR 101.30(a)). Section 403(q) of the FD&C Act. Labeling fails to bear the required nutrition information. No serving size based on the appropriate reference amount customarily consumed (RACC) (21 CFR 101.9(b)(2)). Bottle label declares a serving size as 100g; according to 101.12(b) Table 2. Label does not meet the requirements in section 21 CFR 101.9

records.notes: VIOLATION (IN NOTES): 1. 403(q) 1. The articles are subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801 (a)(3) in that they appear to be misbranded within the meaning of 403(q) because: • The serving size declaration is not expressed in a common household measure as required by 21 CFR 101.9(b)(5) and 21 CFR 101.12(b). In addition, the declared serving size is incorrect; it should be the amount to make 240 ml (8fl oz) and the nutrition value must be based on this serving size. Therefore, the "Serving per container" may also need to be corrected. • The Caloric content is not declared in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(c)(1). Specifically, the caloric content should be declared as "Calories" and the units should be in calories, not "kcal." The "Energy Content" may be expressed in kilojoule units, parenthetically following the statement of caloric content. • There is no established Daily Valve (DV) for trans fat; therefore, a %DV for trans fat cannot be declared in the Nutrition Facts" panel [21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii)]. • The mandatory nutrients, vitamin A, calcium and iron are not declared as required by 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8). • The Total Carbohydrate content is not expressed to the nearest gram [21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)] • The Sugar content is not expressed to the nearest gram [21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)(ii)]. • The nutrition label does not meet the formatting requirements of21 CFR 101.9(d).

Each ingredient must be declared by its common or usual name, as required by 21 CFR 101.4(a). The term “Taste Blender” is not a common or usual name for “Spices” or “Flavoring”. “hydrolyzed vegetable protein” and “natural and nature identical (shrimp)” are not appropriate common or usual name of an ingredient; “edible” is not part of the common or usual name of vegetable oil (21 CFR 102.22).

records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to section 801(a)(3)for the following: It appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(q)(1)(A) because the serving size declared on the label is incorrect. Serving size for a dietary supplement is the maximum amount consumed per eating occasion as recommended on the product label as defined in 21 CFR 101.9(b) and 21 CFR 101.12(b) Table 2. The "Suggested use" states to take 2-6 capsules daily and the Serving Size is identified as 3 capsules. It appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(q)(5)(F) of the Act (21 U.S.C. 343 (q)(5)(F)) in that the presentation of the nutrition information on the labeling of your product does not comply with 21 CFR 101.36. Specifically, the label lists a "Proprietary blend" but fails to list all of the ingredients of the blend. It appears to be misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(e)(2) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(e)(2)] because it fails to bear an accurate statement of the net quantity of contents in terms of weight, measure, or numerical count on the principal display panel as required by 21 CPR 101.105. It appears to be misbranded within the meaning of Section 403(y) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(y)] in that the label fails to bear a domestic address or domestic phone number through which the responsible person (as described in section 761) may receive a report of a serious adverse event with such dietary supplement. It appears to be misbranded within the meaning of section 403(f) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(f)] because the product label contains information in two languages, but does not repeat all the required information in both languages, as required by 21 CFR 101.15(c).

records.product_code: 53 J - - 01 Bath Soaps and Detergents (not Antiperspirant) (Personal Cleanliness)
records.notes: Based on the product labeling, the article, "Tetmosol Medicated Soap," is a "drug" as defined by section 201(g)(1) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1), because it is an article (other than food) intended to cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent disease and/or to affect the structure or function of the body. Specifically, this product is intended for the treatment of one more diseases, including rashes caused by scabies.; Therefore, this product appears to be a new drug within the meaning of section 201(p) of the Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(p) because this product is not generally recognized as safe and effective under the conditions prescribed, recommended or suggested in the labeling. According to section 502(f)(1) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(f)(1), a drug is misbranded if, among other things, it fails to bear adequate directions for its intended use. "Adequate directions for use" are directions under which a layperson can use a drug safely and for the purposes for which it is intended (21 CFR 201.5). Prescription drugs, as defined by section 503(b)(1)(A), of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 353(b)(1)(A), can only be used safely at the direction, and under the supervision, of a licensed practitioner. "Tetmosol Medicated Soap" is intended for the treatment of one or more diseases that are not amenable to self-diagnosis or treatment without the supervision of a licensed practitioner. Thus, it is impossible to write adequate directions for a layperson to use this product safely for its intended purposes. Accordingly, the labeling for "Tetmosol Medicated Soap" fails to bear adequate directions for its intended use and, therefore, the product is misbranded under section 502(f)(1) of the FD&C Act.

records.firm_address: Jeremie Street , Castries, SAINT LUCIA
records.product_code: 54 F - - -- Herbal & Botanicals(other than teas)
records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) of the Act in that it appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(s)(2)(B) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(s)(2)(B)] in that it does not include a statement of identity as a "dietary supplement" as required by 21CFR101.3(g). Sections 403(s)(2)(A) and 403(q)(5)(F) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(s)(2)(A) and 343(q)(5)(F)] in that the LBL fails to list the name of each dietary ingredient of the supplement described in sections 201(ff) and the quantity of each ingredient. Section 403(q)(1)(B) of the Act [21 U.S.C. §343(q)(1)(B)] in that the LBL fails to list the servings per container in accordance with 21 CFR 101.36(b)(1)(ii). Section 403(e)(1) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343 (e)(1)] in that it fails to list the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor in accordance with 21CFR101.5. Section 403(y) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(y)] in that the LBL fails to bear a domestic address or domestic phone number through which the responsible person may receive a report of a serious adverse event with such dietary supplement. Section 403(i)(2) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343 (i)(2)] in that it is fabricated from two or more ingredients, and each ingredient is not declared on the LBL by the common/usual name, in accordance with 21CFR101.4 and 21CFR101.36. Section 403(s)(2)(C) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(s)(2)(C)] in that the LBL fails to identify the part of the plant from which each botanical dietary ingredient in the product is derived, as required by 21CFR101.4(h)(1). Section 403(q)(1)(A) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(q)(1)(A)] in that the serving size on the LBL is incomplete. Specifically, the LBL fails to declare the equivalent metric quantity in parenthesis following the "capful". Section 403(a)(1) of the Act [21 U.S.C. § 343(a)(1)] in that the FDA disclaimer statement is incomplete and not linked to the structure function claim made on the LBL, per 21 CFR 101.93(c)-(d)

records.notes: All low-acid canned foods products FDA conducted an inspection of this aseptically filled and packaged low-acid food manufacturing facility finding serious deviations of the of the Emergency Permit Control regulation (21 CFR Part 108), and the Thermally Processed Low-Acid Foods Packaged in Hermetically Sealed Containers regulation (21 CFR 113). Based on FDA’s inspectional findings and the firm’s inadequate response to findings, all low-acid canned food products processed in the facility appear adulterated within the meaning of section 402(a)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Specific violations include: 21 CFR 108.35(c)(2) – the firm has not filed scheduled process. Labeling an LACF product as “Keep refrigerated” is not an adequate control measure, as refrigeration may slow microbial growth but does not eliminate the risk of C. botulinum as spores can survive at low temperatures and can reactivate if the product is subjected to temperature abuse during distribution or storage. 21 CFR 113.83 – scheduled processes for low-acid foods were not established by qualified persons having expert knowledge of thermal processing requirements for low-acid foods in hermetically sealed containers. records.notes: The article is subject to refusal of admission pursuant to Section 801(a)(3) in that the product appears to be misbranded within the meaning of: Section 403(a)(1) of the Act. Label is false and misleading. Specifically, ingredient is declared in the ingredient statement, it is not appropriate to use a “may contain” statement for the same ingredient. The “may contain” statement may cause consumer confusion. Section 403(q) of the Act. Nutrition facts information is not as defined (21 CFR 101.9). The percent DV for protein, if declared, must be the corrected amount of protein and calculated per 21 CFR 101.9(c)(7)(ii). Based on the ingredient list, it does not appear to have any ingredients that have a protein efficiency ratio (PER) similar to casein. The use of two (2) asterisks for the percent Daily Value (%DV) declaration for sodium is not provided for in 21 CFR 101.9(d)(7)(ii). The quantitative amount for calcium must use the units of measurement and the levels of significance given in 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iii) and 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iv). The %DV for iron not expressed in accordance with 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iii). The label declares 2 mg of iron and the Reference Daily Intake (RDI) for iron is 18 mg. Section 403(f) of the Act. Label contains information in a second language; therefore, all required information must be in all languages (i.e., the English language as well as all foreign languages) represented on the label (21 CFR 101.15(c)(2)). Section 403(i)(2) of the Act. Product is fabricated using an “oil” which is not the common or usual name for any ingredient (21 CFR 101.4(b)(14)), the oil ingredient of a food intended for human consumption must be declared by its specific common or usual name (e.g., “beef fat,” “cottonseed oil”). Section 403(e)(2) of the Act. ZNet Weight is not declared on the principal display panel in terms of avoirdupois pound and ounce (21 CFR 101.7(a) and 101.7(b)(1))

"Honey" is declared as part of the statement of identity located on the principal display panel for both products. The information panel located on the back of the packages appear to declare the products as a "honey syrup." • The information panel on the back of the packages state that the product is "honey syrup." The statement of identity, ingredient statement and net quantity must be declared in all of the foreign languages and English (21 CFR 101.15(c)(2)). Section 403(i)(1) of the Act.
